title: Can AI-generated characters be rigged automatically, or do they need cleanup first?
author: Excellent-Worry-85
selftext:
fixing elbows at midnight, not fun, I have been there, more than once lol. a character can often be rigged automatically, but the rig is only as good as the mesh underneath it. if the topology is uneven, if parts overlap, or if the pose is not close to a T pose, the automatic weights can pull the wrong areas when the character moves

do that check first, it can save a lot of wasted effort. Tripo Studio offers auto rigging with a rig check and a T pose option, and it can export in a format that works with common humanoid rigging services for Unity or Unreal. that can give a starting rig, and the rig check can show whether the model is ready for rigging at all

topology and pose, thats what a rig check can hinge on. checking whether the model passes that step first can show where cleanup may be needed before rigging. skip it, and you are guessing, I skipped it once and spent the night fixing elbows, never again

generation and rigging are only a starting point, it may still need retopology, mesh repair, part splitting and manual weight cleanup before it can be animated. the amount of cleanup can hinge on character shape, input views, and intended use. did yours pass a rig check first?

comments.author: Itchy_Ship2584

they need cleanup first

good news: AI (astra, fable, neon) can clean them up (mostly)
